title: Thanking
subtitle: ありがとう
review: Written by Claude. The Japanese and the romaji have not been checked by a Japanese speaker. English support only: no Burmese lines were written. Check before recording audio.

categories.desc: From the polite standard to a quick thanks between friends.
cards: Arigatō gozaimasu.
Thank you.

ありがとうございます。

The safe, polite thank you, for anyone.

Tetsudatte kurete, arigatō gozaimasu.
手伝ってくれて、ありがとうございます。
Thank you for helping me.
Arigatō.
Thanks.

ありがとう。

Casual: friends and family only.

Purezento, arigatō!
プレゼント、ありがとう！
Thanks for the present!
Dōmo arigatō gozaimasu.
Thank you very much.

どうもありがとうございます。

Dōmo makes it warmer. Dōmo on its own is a quick, light thanks.

Kyō wa dōmo arigatō gozaimashita.
今日はどうもありがとうございました。
Thank you very much for today.
Arigatō gozaimashita.
Thank you (for what you did).

ありがとうございました。

The past form: the help or the service is over, as when you leave a shop or a class.

Sensei, arigatō gozaimashita.
先生、ありがとうございました。
Thank you, teacher.

categories.desc: Japanese answers to thanks are modest: mostly a way of saying no.
cards: Dō itashimashite.
You're welcome.

どういたしまして。

The textbook answer. A little formal in daily life.

Arigatō gozaimasu. — Dō itashimashite.
ありがとうございます。— どういたしまして。
Thank you. — You're welcome.
Iie, iie.
Not at all.

いいえ、いいえ。

Literally 'no, no': the modest everyday answer.

Tasukarimashita. — Iie, iie.
助かりました。— いいえ、いいえ。
You were a great help. — Not at all.
Kochira koso.
The pleasure is mine.

こちらこそ。

'It is I who should thank you.' It hands the thanks back.

Kyō wa arigatō gozaimashita. — Kochira koso.
今日はありがとうございました。— こちらこそ。
Thank you for today. — Thank you.
Tondemo nai desu.
Not at all.

とんでもないです。

Stronger and more polite than iie: 'far from it'.

Hontō ni arigatō gozaimashita. — Tondemo nai desu.
本当にありがとうございました。— とんでもないです。
Thank you so much. — Not at all.

categories.desc: Set phrases that carry thanks: for help, for food, for someone's trouble.
cards: Sumimasen.
Thank you (for your trouble).

すみません。

Japanese often thank with 'sorry', when someone has gone out of their way for you.

A, sumimasen.
あ、すみません。
Oh, thank you. (someone picks up what you dropped)
Tasukarimashita.
That was a great help.

助かりました。

'I was saved.' After someone has helped you.

Hontō ni tasukarimashita.
本当に助かりました。
You really helped me out.
Itadakimasu.
(said before eating)

いただきます。

'I humbly receive.' Said before every meal: thanks for the food.

Oishisō! Itadakimasu.
おいしそう！いただきます。
That looks delicious! Let's eat.
Gochisōsama deshita.
Thank you for the meal.

ごちそうさまでした。

Said after eating: to the cook, to your host, or to the restaurant staff as you leave.

Gochisōsama deshita. Oishikatta desu.
ごちそうさまでした。おいしかったです。
Thank you for the meal. It was delicious.
